posting.headline: IT Manager (phone management and daily tech fixes), Cairo
posting.about: We run video recording teams at factories, warehouses, farms, and construction sites across Cairo. Workers wear a small camera on a cap while they do their normal job. Every camera is a phone, and every phone is managed through Hexnode. You run it: you enrol every phone, see where each one is, lock one that goes missing, and fix the daily tech problems of the people on the floor.
do: Enrol every new phone in Hexnode and put its label on. A phone we cannot see does not go to a site.
Keep the device list matching the phone registry: same tags, same sites, same count.
Keep location tracking on: a position every 45 minutes, and live the moment a phone reconnects.
Control phones from your screen: install apps, change settings, restart, and check a screen remotely.
Put a missing phone in lost mode within the hour. Wipe it when told, never before.
Fix the daily tech problems of operators and Portfolio Managers: a login, an upload, a setting.
Keep the two test phones. Every app update goes to them first, and to the fleet after a full test shift.
Give the MDM number for the Thursday count. Chase every phone missing from the map the same day.
need: You have managed phones or computers for a company before, with a management tool.
Careful with a list. Every phone has a tag, a row, and a dot on the map.
Patient on the phone with someone who is not technical and is in a hurry.
Fast when a phone goes missing. Lost mode within the hour, every time.
plus: You have used Hexnode or another mobile device management tool.
You have supported people in the field, not only in an office.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
One tool, one fleet, and one list that is yours to keep clean.
Every procedure written down: enrolment, the missing phone, the update, and the count.
A direct line to the CTO, who owns the technology.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and the fleets or tools you have managed. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of IT Manager at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the CTO.
Your start date is {start}. In your first weeks you take over Hexnode, match the device list to the registry, and enrol your first batch of phones. {manager} checks your work.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours, and every hour comes from a phone. Hexnode is how we see every phone, lock it, and control it from anywhere, including the ones at delivery partners. You run it. A phone that is not on the map, a stale location, or a tech problem that stops someone filming is yours to fix the same day.
outcomes: Every phone the company owns shows on the map with its tag and its site.
The device list matches the registry every Thursday.
A missing phone is in lost mode within the hour.
No update reaches the fleet before the two test phones pass a full test shift.
daily: Morning. Open Hexnode. Every phone that should be online is online, with a position from the last 45 minutes. A phone dark since last night: call its Portfolio Manager.
All day. Tech problems from operators and Portfolio Managers: a login, an upload, a setting, a phone that will not restart. Fix it from your screen first. Go to the site if you cannot.
Same day. New phones from the Inventory Manager: enrol, label, lock the collection app as the only app, and check the registry row matches. Hand them back for the test recording.
Same hour. A missing phone. Find it on the map, put it in lost mode, and tell Moharam and its Portfolio Manager. Nobody wipes it yet.
Within 24 hours. A phone still missing after 24 hours is wiped when Mazen tells you. Mark it lost in the device list.
Test phones. Look at the two test phones for a new version of the collection app. A new version means a full test shift before anyone else gets it.
weekly: Thursday, before 4:00 PM. Clean the device list for the weekly count: every phone on the map, tag matching its registry row. Send Mazen the MDM number.
Once a week. Go through the week's fixes with Youssif: what broke, what keeps breaking, and what to change on the phones.
Once a week. Check the partner phones: every one on the map, every one sending a position. A partner phone gone dark goes to Moharam.
monthly: Month end. Go through the month's app versions and settings with Youssif. Agree on what changes next month.
Month end. Retire what cannot be repaired: wipe it, remove it from Hexnode, and tell Mazen to close its row.
standards: Every phone is enrolled before it is tagged, and tagged before it joins a kit. A phone we cannot see does not go to a site.
The collection app is the only app the phone runs. Nobody installs anything on a phone but you.
Location tracking stays on: every 45 minutes, and live the moment a phone reconnects.
Lost mode within the hour. Wipe only after 24 hours, and only when Mazen or Moharam tells you.
Every update goes to the two test phones first, always. The fleet gets it only after a full test shift passes.
The device list and the registry say the same number. Any gap is found the same day.
An app bug goes to Youssif, never to the client. Money to Ahmed Alaa, papers to Mano.
never: Never wipe first. Find it, lock it, wait 24 hours, then wipe. A wiped phone cannot be found.
Never send an update to the fleet before the two test phones pass a full test shift.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name or the app's name outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: Hexnode with Youssif: every phone, every setting, the map, lost mode, and the device list. The store with Mazen: the registry and the tags.
Match the device list to the registry, phone by phone. Take every tech call from operators and Portfolio Managers yourself.
Enrol one full batch of phones for a new site, and run one update through the two test phones. Youssif checks your work.
A Thursday count where the device list matches the registry, tag by tag. Youssif signs you off.

measures: Phones on the map with a position from the last 45 minutes, every day.
Minutes from a phone reported missing to lost mode. Under 60, every time.
Thursday counts where the device list matched the registry.
Tech problems fixed the same day, and the ones that came back.
handbook.call: Youssif, for Hexnode, an app bug, or anything you cannot fix. Mazen for the registry, the tags, and any phone that moves. Moharam for a missing phone and anything on the floor. Ahmed Alaa for money. Mano for papers. An injury or the police: Moharam, then Adham.
